card.summary: The Prevent Government Shutdowns Act automatically provides temporary funding to prevent government shutdowns if regular appropriations bills are not enacted before a new fiscal year begins. During this funding lapse, the bill restricts official travel and campaign funds for official travel by Members of Congress and certain federal employees, limits legislative business and recesses in Congress, and requires daily quorum calls.

summary: The Prevent Government Shutdowns Act of 2026 provides automatic temporary funding for federal programs, projects, and activities if regular appropriations bills are not enacted before a new fiscal year begins. It provides funding in 14-day increments at the rate of operations from the prior fiscal year. It also restricts official travel, campaign fund usage for official travel, and congressional recesses, and limits the consideration of unrelated legislation for members of Congress and certain federal employees during periods of automatic continuing appropriations.

affected_groups.effect: Receive automatic temporary funding in 14-day increments based on the previous fiscal year's funding levels when regular appropriations lapse.

Face strict limitations on official travel, bans on using campaign funds for official travel, restrictions on recesses exceeding 23 hours, and limitations on considering unrelated legislation during funding lapses.
affected_groups.group: Members of Congress and congressional staff

affected_groups.effect: Subject to the same official travel limitations as congressional staff during periods of automatic continuing appropriations.
affected_groups.group: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) employees

key_provisions: Provides automatic continuing appropriations for federal programs in 14-day increments if full-year or regular appropriations are not enacted by the start of the fiscal year.
Sets funding rates based on the preceding fiscal year's operations and restricts high initial rates of operation or certain grant awards that impinge on final funding prerogatives.

Prohibits the obligation or expenditure of funds for official travel by Members of Congress, congressional staff, and OMB employees during a period of automatic continuing appropriations, with narrow exceptions for returning to Washington, D.C., local travel within the National Capital Region, and national security events.
Restricts the use of campaign contributions or donations for official travel by federal officeholders during periods of automatic continuing appropriations.
Prohibits the Senate and House of Representatives from moving to recess or adjourn for more than 23 hours during a lapse in appropriations.

Restricts floor proceedings during a lapse in appropriations primarily to measures making appropriations, addressing the public debt limit, or certain high-level nominations and expired program extensions after 30 days.
Requires a two-thirds supermajority vote in either House of Congress to waive the procedural restrictions on floor actions or recesses.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Prevent Government Shutdowns Act of 2026 provides automatic temporary funding for federal programs, projects, and activities if regular appropriations bills are not enacted before a new fiscal year begins. It provides funding in 14-day increments at the rate of operations from the prior fiscal year. It also restricts official travel, campaign fund usage for official travel, and congressional recesses, and limits the consideration of unrelated legislation for members of Congress and certain federal employees during periods of automatic continuing appropriations.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a permanent mechanism to automatically prevent federal government shutdowns by enacting temporary funding every 14 days during budget impasses, while simultaneously imposing severe procedural and travel restrictions on Congress and OMB personnel to incentivize timely completion of the regular appropriations process.
